overall_summary: Bitcoin is under clear near-term pressure from record ETF outflows and a hawkish macro setup that has locked in December Fed hike bets while the dollar holds firm. Middle East flashpoints add another risk-off layer for crypto and broader markets. Extreme fear readings and steady whale accumulation offer some contrarian cushion, but the forward catalysts still lean negative.
key_points: Record ETF outflows push Bitcoin under $60K
Hot PCE and GDP lock in Fed hike bets
Strong dollar and global hikes weigh on risk
Middle East tensions lift oil and risk-off tone
Extreme fear plus whale buying show capitulation bid

items.title: Bitcoin Slips Below $60K as ETF Outflows Hit Record $5.8B
items.summary: Bitcoin fell back under sixty thousand dollars on Friday, missing a strong Wall Street rebound after Thanksgiving, and traded near fifty-nine thousand into the weekend. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about three hundred eighty-nine million dollars leave on Friday, the eighth straight outflow day, pushing November's total to a record roughly five point seven eight billion. BlackRock's IBIT led the redemptions. Traders should care because sustained institutional outflows remove a key bid and keep pressure on price while stocks diverge higher.
items.impact: Continued selling pressure and weaker institutional demand near key levels

items.title: Whales Add 121,000 BTC in Q4 Despite Nearly 30% Drop
items.summary: CryptoQuant data shows addresses holding one thousand to ten thousand Bitcoin added about one hundred twenty-one thousand BTC between late September and mid-November even as price fell roughly thirty percent. That reversed the usual fourth-quarter selling pattern seen in seven of the prior nine years, though unrealized profits for large holders collapsed about eighty-one percent to twenty-three point eight billion dollars. Traders should watch this because heavy accumulation by big wallets during a washout has historically preceded stronger recoveries if selling exhausts.
items.impact: Potential basing signal if whale buying absorbs ETF and retail supply

items.title: Nearly $7 Billion Bitcoin Options Expire on Deribit
items.summary: About six point eight to seven billion dollars notional in Bitcoin options expired Friday on Deribit, roughly a quarter of open interest, with a put-call ratio near zero point eight nine showing heavy downside hedging. Max pain sat around seventy thousand while Bitcoin settled near sixty-one thousand six hundred before sliding lower. The event coincided with thin holiday liquidity and the drop under sixty thousand. Traders care because large expiries can free up hedges and amplify moves once positioning rolls off, and the defensive skew signals caution into year-end.
items.impact: Post-expiry volatility risk with lingering defensive options positioning

items.title: Trump-Linked WLFI Token Plunges Over 50% After ETH Dump
items.summary: World Liberty Financial's WLFI token crashed more than fifty percent to record lows near one point six cents after a project-linked strategic reserve wallet sold roughly twelve thousand ETH for about twenty million dollars at a nearly nineteen million dollar loss. Proceeds moved toward lending platforms amid speculation over debt or collateral needs, and long liquidations piled up. Traders should note it because high-profile political crypto projects can spill sentiment risk across the market and highlight liquidity and governance stress in altcoins.
items.impact: Negative sentiment spillover and heightened altcoin liquidation risk

items.title: Binance Fully Lifts Post-Hack Withdrawal Suspensions
items.summary: Binance announced it has completed recovery work and fully lifted the withdrawal suspension tied to October's roughly six point three billion dollar hack, with withdrawals open across nearly all networks four weeks later. A few networks remain paused only for routine maintenance. The exchange previously covered losses with its own funds. Traders should care because restoring full functionality at the largest exchange reduces operational risk premium and can support confidence and flows after a major security scare.
items.impact: Improved exchange confidence and reduced friction for capital movement

items.title: Crypto Fear and Greed Index Hits Extreme Fear at 10
items.summary: The Crypto Fear and Greed Index sank to ten amid Bitcoin's drop below sixty thousand, heavy ETF outflows, and long liquidations totaling hundreds of millions. Market value sat near two point zero seven trillion with open interest also contracting. Extreme readings like this often mark washed-out conditions rather than the start of fresh selling. Traders watch it because capitulation-level fear has frequently aligned with local bottoms when paired with on-chain accumulation, though confirmation still needs price structure and flow improvement.
items.impact: Oversold backdrop that can support a bounce if support holds

items.title: Hot PCE and 4.3% GDP Lock In December Fed Hike
items.summary: October core PCE came in at 3.3 percent year-over-year, a touch above forecasts and the highest in years, while third-quarter GDP was revised sharply higher to 4.3 percent annualized. Markets have fully priced a 25 basis point Federal Reserve hike at the December 9 meeting, with solid odds of more tightening into early 2027. For crypto traders this keeps financial conditions tight and supports a firm dollar, which has historically weighed on Bitcoin and risk assets until the path peaks.
items.impact: Supports higher US yields and DXY, pressure on BTC and risk assets

items.title: Dollar Holds Near Multi-Month Highs on Hike Bets
items.summary: The US Dollar Index closed Friday around 104 after touching a 20-to-22-month peak earlier in the week near 104.5. Strong growth and sticky inflation data kept December hike odds near 100 percent even as markets digested AI-related equity swings over the holiday-shortened week. A firm greenback and elevated short-end yields typically act as a headwind for Bitcoin by tightening global liquidity and making dollar assets more attractive.
items.impact: Firm DXY and yields continue to constrain crypto upside

items.title: US Goods Trade Deficit Widens Sharply on Import Surge
items.summary: Friday’s advance data showed the October goods trade deficit ballooning to 149.5 billion dollars from 135 billion, far wider than expected, as imports jumped more than 21 billion while exports rose more modestly. Capital goods imports were especially strong. Wholesale inventories also rose 0.9 percent, beating forecasts. The print is mixed for growth signals but can influence dollar and rate expectations heading into next week’s quieter data calendar before NFP.
items.impact: Mixed growth/dollar signal ahead of December jobs and FOMC

items.title: Tokyo Core CPI Hits 16-Month High, Supports BOJ Talk
items.summary: Tokyo’s core consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 2.9 percent year-over-year in November, the fastest in 16 months, driven largely by the end of energy subsidies. Underlying measures eased slightly. The reading keeps alive discussion of a possible Bank of Japan rate increase in December and adds another hawkish central-bank voice globally. Yen strength or higher Japanese rates can ripple into dollar pairs and risk sentiment that crypto traders watch.
items.impact: Potential BOJ tightening adds to global rate pressure

items.title: France and Spain Inflation Cool More Than Expected
items.summary: Preliminary November readings showed French HICP falling to 3.2 percent and Spanish HICP to 4.1 percent, both well below forecasts, as energy prices eased. Core measures also softened. Soft prints offer some relief but come against still-hawkish ECB October minutes that showed many members ready to hike earlier, plus near-certain December action. For markets this slightly eases euro-area rate fears while the leadership transition to Pablo Hernandez de Cos begins to take shape.
items.impact: Mildly eases ECB hike intensity but December move still priced

items.title: Bank of Korea Hikes to 3.25 Percent on Chip Boom
items.summary: South Korea’s central bank raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 3.25 percent and sharply upgraded growth forecasts on the back of the AI-driven semiconductor export surge. Inflation remains above target and the board left the door open to further moves. The decision adds to the list of major central banks still tightening and underscores how AI-related strength is feeding into global rate paths that matter for dollar liquidity and crypto.
items.impact: Another major central bank tightening supports higher global rates

items.title: US Disables Ship Breaching Iran Blockade; Tehran Vows Hormuz Stay Shut
items.summary: US Central Command says American aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged bulk carrier Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman after it left Bandar Abbas and ignored warnings, disabling its propulsion with the crew unharmed. This is at least the sixth vessel disabled since the blockade resumed and the fifteenth overall. Iranian officials, including a supreme leader adviser and the navy chief, vow to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed and break the US embargo, while IRGC claims of mines hitting tankers add to shipping fears. Traders should care because Hormuz carries a huge share of global oil; disruptions keep Brent elevated near ninety-five dollars and fuel risk-off moves across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Heightened oil supply risk and geopolitical premium pressure risk assets

items.title: Iranian-Made Drone Kills Two Italian Technicians in Kuwait
items.summary: Italy’s foreign minister confirms two Rheinmetall Italia technicians died from debris after Kuwait intercepted drones of Iranian origin targeting a vital military air-defence site. The workers were maintaining Skyguard radar systems; a Kuwaiti and Pakistani were also injured. Iran denies launching the attack and offers a joint probe, while calling the incident suspicious. This marks the first European civilian deaths tied to the wider US-Iran conflict and raises the odds of further Gulf escalation that can spike energy prices and volatility for risk assets.
items.impact: Regional escalation risk lifts oil premium and risk-off pressure

items.title: Houthis Hit Saudi Oil Sites and Riyadh as Allies Rally Support
items.summary: Yemen’s Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery and other infrastructure, with satellite images showing smoke and temporary operational halts reported at facilities including Jazan. Earlier hits damaged the PIF tower in Riyadh’s financial district and injured civilians. Pakistan and Turkey pledged support to Saudi Arabia under a defense pact treating an attack on one as an attack on all. Persistent threats to the world’s top oil exporter and export terminals keep energy markets jumpy and support a geopolitical risk premium that weighs on broader risk appetite.
items.impact: Oil infrastructure threats sustain supply fears and market volatility

items.title: Zelensky Calls Trump-Putin 'Friend' Remark Strange, Urges Pressure
items.summary: In a BBC interview, Ukrainian President Zelensky said it is strange that US President Trump called Vladimir Putin 'my friend' after their China summit embrace, comparing it to befriending Hitler in World War Two and calling Putin an aggressor and killer. He urged Washington to apply more pressure on Moscow and noted peace talks remain fruitless so far. EU leaders have struggled to agree new large-scale funding for Ukraine. The friction highlights uncertainty over Western support and the path to any ceasefire, which can swing risk sentiment depending on whether talks advance or stall.
items.impact: Aid and diplomacy uncertainty keeps geopolitical overhang unresolved

items.title: Taiwan Votes in Local Elections as China Watches Closely
items.summary: Taiwan held nine-in-one local elections on November 28 for mayors, magistrates and thousands of other posts across 22 cities and counties, plus a nuclear power referendum. Results are a mid-term test for President Lai’s DPP ahead of the 2028 presidential race, with key contests in Taipei and other big cities. China has denounced certain candidates and stepped up military activity nearby. While the races focus on local issues, outcomes can signal the political balance on cross-strait policy and influence investor views of Taiwan risk and semiconductor supply chains.
items.impact: Political signal for 2028 and cross-strait tension; markets await full results

items.title: Israeli Strike Kills Two MSF Staff at Marked Gaza Clinic
items.summary: Doctors Without Borders said an Israeli strike scored a direct hit on one of its clearly marked Gaza City clinics, killing two watchmen and bringing its staff death toll in Gaza to seventeen. MSF stated the location had been communicated to the Israeli military. The IDF said the two men were Hamas military wing members acting as guards and that the strike was not aimed at a hospital or medical infrastructure. The incident draws international condemnation and keeps Middle East tensions elevated even as the larger Iran and Gulf stories dominate energy markets.
items.impact: Sustains regional volatility without immediate new oil catalyst
